newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar rebounds, may re-test upside overnight.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar rebounds, may re-test upside overnight.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar rebounded on Tuesday, recouping most of its earlier losses and re-setting itself for another possible upside push.
The currency ended at US$0.6980/87 and at 66.40 on the Trade Weighted Index Index from 0.6983/90, 66.42 early in the session, having sunk to a low of 0.6956.

Dealers said the weakness was brought on by the market being long in anticipation of renewed Japanese interest. When that failed to materialise, the currency sunk to 0.6970 afterwhich stop-loss orders drove it lower.
Short covering, possibly by an offshore buyer, then saw the currency rebound.
"The stops have been taken out and the buyers have come back in, pushing us back up to that 0.6980 level," said one senior Wellington dealer.
Support now appeared to be around 0.6950-60.

"I guess we'll go back and try and see what the resistance is like back at 0.6985-90. It may traverse that 60-90 range and we may have a go at the topside to see what's going on," he said. Overnight, dealers expect a 0.6960-90 range.
An Auckland dealer also expected an upward bias, but for players to be more wary after the sudden dip.
"People will be a bit cautious of it next time around unless you see further investment come through from the Japanese," he said.
